name: AD845
tagline: ADI's 16 MHz, 100 V/µs JFET single from c. 1990. One headphone survey found it smooth and slightly valve-like.

lineage.note: Sole source. 12/90 Rev. A SPICE models imply a graded datasheet by then. Complementary bipolar process.
Non-Z JN/KN reportedly discontinued under PDN 10_0081; Pb-free JNZ/KNZ still listed by distributors.

part_numbers.note: Family name. ADI product page exists; lifecycle unconfirmed. Datasheet current Rev. E.
J grade, 0–70 °C, PDIP-8. JN reportedly discontinued; JNZ at RS UK (5229464).
K (best) grade, 0–70 °C, PDIP-8. KN reportedly replaced by KNZ (PDN 10_0081).
J grade, 16-lead wide SOIC, not SOIC-8. REEL variants only in third-party lists.
A grade, −40 to +85 °C. Orderable codes (e.g. AQ) not seen.
B grade, −40 to +85 °C. BQ (CERDIP by convention) only in third-party lists.
S grade, −55 to +125 °C. SQ variants third-party only; no 5962 SMD seen.

key_specs.value: 4 µV p-p max (1 kHz density not captured)
16 MHz typ, 12.8 MHz min; AOL 250 V/mV min
N-channel JFET pair on complementary bipolar (CBFET)
key_specs.source: Datasheet Rev. E; ADI SPICE ad845.cir

reputation.summary: Thin enthusiast coverage. The only listening report is a 2005 DiyEden survey translated on Soomal. It calls the AD845 smooth and slightly valve-like with ADI punch, looser and 'slower' than Burr-Brown. It ranks resolution above OPA132/134 and AD823, below AD843 and OPA627, and suits mains-powered amps. A 'cult following' for DAC I/V is unsourced.
caveats: All listening impressions come from one translated reviewer's survey.
Single only; SOIC is 16-lead wide body (AD845JR-16), not SOIC-8.
About 10 mA quiescent current (reviewer): poor for battery amps.
Needs ±4.75 V minimum; reviewer measured 8.7 V (0.5 V into 33 Ω), 9.0 V (2 V into 330 Ω).
Fast part (100 V/µs, 16 MHz): normal high-speed layout and decoupling care applies.

counterfeit_notes: No AD845 fakes reported. Check logo, grade letter, date code. SOIC-8 'AD845' is suspect (real SOIC is 16-lead). Expect ~10 mA, ~100 V/µs, ≥12.8 MHz; a relabelled TL071 draws far less. Non-Z JN/KN carry pre-2010 codes.

refuted_claims: 'CBFET' unverified: wrong. Datasheet title is 'Precision, 16 MHz CBFET Op Amp' on ADI's complementary bipolar process.
Non-Z AD845KN not seen: wrong. alldatasheet lists AD845KN, and a PDN reportedly names AD845KNZ as its replacement.
Whole series discontinued: unsupported. Only non-Z JN/KN were replaced; RS UK and Digi-Key still list the part.
corrections: Technology confirmed as CBFET: N-JFET input on complementary bipolar.
